source.extractionTool: pdftotext (poppler), -enc UTF-8, raw and -layout modes, page-by-page
source.notes: Single PDF (code 'T27 521 – SPECIMEN', printed footer) contains both the Question Paper (19 printed pages = PDF pages 1-19) and a 'DRAFT MARKING SCHEME' (6 printed pages = PDF pages 20-25); page numbers below are PDF page numbers, which equal the printed page numbers. Found on the official specimen-papers listing page https://cisce.org/specimen-question-papers-icse-class-x-2027/ ; the specimen is published for the ICSE 2027 examination, so examYear is 2027. Maximum Marks 80, Time allowed Two hours (2027 specimen papers use a 2-hour Section-A/Section-B format rather than the older 1hr45min format); first 15 minutes are reading time only. Official ExamReady field 'session' set to a descriptive label because no exam session (e.g. 'March 2027') is printed. Structure: SECTION A (40 Marks) is compulsory - Question 1 (15 one-mark MCQ/assertion-reason sub-parts (i)-(xv)), Question 2 ([6] one-mark fill-in-the-blank sub-parts under (i), plus a 2-mark match-the-column (ii) and a 2-mark figure-based (iii)), and Question 3 (seven 2- or 3-mark sub-questions (i)-(vii)). SECTION B (40 Marks) prints 'Attempt any four questions from this Section' and offers six 10-mark questions (Question 4 - Question 9); this pack extracts ALL SIX Section B questions (60 marks) because the choice is of whole questions, not internal alternatives, so the pack's marks total (100) intentionally exceeds maxMarks (80) - a student scores at most 80 by answering 40 (Section A) + 40 (best 4 of 6 Section B questions, 10 each). No question in this paper prints an internal-choice 'OR' between alternative sub-parts, so choiceGroup is null throughout. Many marking-scheme equations/labels use an embedded math-italic font whose glyphs did not map to correct Unicode in the PDF text layer: a genuine variable (e.g. 't', 'v', 'C') consistently extracts as that same character doubled, which was decoded by removing the duplicate; but any word or label (e.g. 'Fulcrum', 'Resistance', 'cm') extracts as a single wrong glyph repeated 2x-the-letter-count times, which is NOT literally recoverable - where the surrounding physics/lever/circuit vocabulary made the intended word unambiguous (matched by letter-count and context, e.g. a 7-repeat-14 run next to '... and effort points' in a lever question decoding to 'Fulcrum'), it was reconstructed and flagged per-question with MEDIUM confidence; otherwise it was left out and flagged. A few marking-scheme cells (e.g. Q3(v)(a), Q5(i)'s diagram, Q8(i)(b)) are graphs/diagrams or were simply blank in the text layer and are flagged as missing rather than guessed. Cognitive-level tags ('[Application]', '[Recall]', etc.) are printed in the right margin of the question paper; on pages where a tag's row could not be matched 1:1 to its sub-part with certainty (rare - only page 3, Question 1 (i)-(iii)), tags were assigned in the same top-to-bottom order as the sub-parts, based on the clean 1:1 pattern observed on every other page of this paper. Usage: Official CISCE publication, freely available on cisce.org; question text reproduced for study with attribution and a link to the original. Figures are not reproduced.

questions.text: A heavy object and a light object are placed on a seesaw. Which arrangement produces the maximum turning effect about the pivot?
options: Both objects near the pivot on opposite sides.
Heavy object close to the pivot; light object at the far end on the opposite side.
Light object close to the pivot; heavy object at the far end on the opposite side.
Both objects at the ends of the seesaw, on opposite sides of pivot.

officialAnswer.text: (c) Light object close to the pivot; heavy object at the far end on the opposite side.

questions.text: A concave lens diverges light because its upper and lower parts act as:

Assertion (A): Blue light scatters more than red light in the atmosphere.
Reason (R): Intensity of scattered light is inversely proportional to the fourth power of wavelength.

Advanced optical sensors in missiles use fibre optic cables to transmit light signals with minimal loss. This relies on a physical phenomenon that confines light within the fibres, making the system very dependable for guiding the missile precisely.
(a) Name the optical phenomenon that allows light signals to remain confined within the fibre optic cables during transmission.
(b) List the two main conditions necessary for this phenomenon to occur.

officialAnswer.text:
(a) Total internal reflection
(b) 1. Light ray should travel from denser to rarer medium.
2. Angle of incidence must be greater than the critical angle for a given pair of optical media.

questions.text:
A metal rod AB of length 80 cm is balanced at 45 cm from the end A with 100 gf weights suspended from the two ends.
(a) If this rod is cut at the centre C, then compare the weight of AC to the weight of BC. (Use >, < or =)
(b) Give a reason for your answer in (a).

officialAnswer.text:
(a) Weight of AC < weight of BC
(b) Even though the weights present are the same at both ends, the torque arm of B is less than the torque arm of A. This indicates that the weight of the rod is concentrated more between C and B than between A and C.

questions.text: A boy is located asymmetrically between two parallel walls, closer to the left wall than the right. If he claps, the time interval between successive echoes is 0.25 s, then find the value of X in metres. [speed of sound in air = 340 m/s.]
extractionIssues: The question text does not state a distance value, but the marking scheme uses a distance of 68 m to the far wall; this is likely given in a diagram/figure not reproduced in the text layer

A short connecting phrase in the marking scheme ('time required for shorter distance i.e for x m') was reconstructed from a corrupted math-font run by matching letter-count and the parallel, uncorrupted first line ('Time required for longer distance i.e 68 m')

officialAnswer.text:

questions.text:
Two wires A and B of the same material and length are fixed to a wooden board and stretched under the same tension. The cross-sectional area of wire A is greater than that of wire B. When set into vibration using identical tuning forks of frequency 300 Hz, only wire B produces a loud sound.
Name and explain the phenomenon responsible for the loud sound produced by wire B.

officialAnswer.text: Resonance. The frequency of the tuning fork (300 Hz) matches the natural frequency of wire B and the amplitude of vibration increases.

questions.text:
Two wires A and B of the same material and length are fixed to a wooden board and stretched under the same tension. The cross-sectional area of wire A is greater than that of wire B. When set into vibration using identical tuning forks of frequency 300 Hz, only wire B produces a loud sound.
A loud sound is heard from wire A when the experiment is repeated using a tuning fork of frequency f. Is 'f' greater than, less than or equal to 300 Hz? Justify your answer.

officialAnswer.text: f < 300 Hz. Wire A is thicker than wire B, therefore its natural frequency is less than that of wire B.
